_readme: Maps dashboard fields onto warehouse columns. Orderwise stores container analysis fields as generic columns (shpca_c_1..10 text, shpca_n_1..10 numeric, shpca_d_1..10 date, shpca_l_1..10 boolean, shpca_m_1..10 memo). Their meaning is set in Orderwise config, not in the SQL, so confirm the assignments below against real data: run the app in BigQuery mode and open /api/inspect, which profiles each column with sample values. Edit this file and redeploy; no code changes needed.
_confirmed: Confirmed against live data 25 Jul 2026: c_1 = UK/domestic port, c_2 = freight forwarder, c_3 = departure port, c_5 = container type (20/40 foot), c_6 = UK delivery address, m_1 = the import team's free-text operational log (populated on 227 of 256 containers, 197 distinct, newest entry first, display and search only, never parsed). Still unconfirmed: PO (left unmapped so it shows blank rather than wrong), supplier (guessed c_7), forwarder ref (guessed c_4). Empty in every row sampled: c_9, c_10, m_2..m_10, n_2..n_10. Unexplained: n_1 holds 30/60/70/75/90 across 200 containers, left unmapped until someone confirms what it means. Confirm via /api/inspect and edit here.

sources._readme: Where a name comes from when both a master record and an analysis column exist. 'master' uses the Orderwise supplier record in supply_detail (container.shpc_sd_id for the supplier, the biggest freight cost line's shpcsm_sd_id for the forwarder). 'analysis' uses the shpca_c_* column mapped below. Either way the other one is the fallback when the preferred source is blank. Supplier defaults to master because the c_7 mapping is only a guess; forwarder defaults to analysis because c_2 is confirmed correct and carries the names the team recognises.

costs._readme: A cost line (shipping method row) counts as freight when its description contains one of these keywords, case-insensitive. Everything else is an add-on. Lines use the invoiced net when present, otherwise the expected cost.

status._readme: Statuses that mean a container is on the water. Used in addition to the date rule (shipped but not yet delivered).

routes._readme: Transit-time surcharges by origin, in weeks. Matched as a case-insensitive substring of the departure port.
